cohort: 220 pregnant women, categorized into obese (n=110) and non-obese (n=110) groups based on pre-pregnancy BMI, at a tertiary care hospital.
finding: Maternal obesity significantly impacts labor and delivery outcomes, leading to increased labor duration, higher intervention rates, and more perinatal and postpartum complications.
mod_finding: Obese women experienced higher rates of cesarean sections and assisted vaginal deliveries, and were less likely to have spontaneous vaginal deliveries.
followup_time: until hospital discharge (average 3.8 to 4.5 days postpartum)
